caption: Loudest bin: the whole matrix coloured by which band is loudest, as bright as it is loud
why: A kick drum, a voice and a hi-hat each sit in a different part of the spectrum. Loudest bin says which part is loudest right now - 0 for bass up to 1 for treble - and how loud it is, so the colour of an effect can follow what is playing: red on the kicks, blue on the hats.
Its neighbours: FFT bin follows one band you choose; Timbre gives the balance of the whole mix; Spectrum gives every band; Loudest bin gives the winner.
steps: Loudest bin has no inputs. **from** is 1 and **to** is 15: it listens to bands 1..15 (band 0, the very lowest rumble, is left out).
`bin` - which band is loudest, 0..1 - is the **Palette**'s index, so the whole matrix takes the colour for that part of the spectrum.
`level` - how loud that band is - lifted by a **Remap** (0..0.5 into 0.15..1) is the brightness, so the matrix is never quite dark.
The trace shows which band wins (orange) jumping between the kick's band and the hats', and its level (grey).

try.label: Ignore the bass
try.text: from 6: only the middle and high bands compete, so the colour follows the melody and the hats.

try.label: Only the bass
try.text: to 4: only the low bands compete - the colour changes with which bass note is loudest.
